Reference

Tracing & metrics

SACI emits structured tracing events, gated behind one feature flag. saci-core emits; saci-service exports. This page is reference: the spans, the config keys, the series and their writers. The two sections "Where instrumentation comes from" and "The spans and events" are explanation, for readers who want the shape of the tree before the exact keys.

In one line
A nested span tree, a fmt subscriber, optional OTLP span export, and a Prometheus endpoint carrying thirty-two series
You need
The tracing feature on saci-core or saci-service; the service feature turns it on for you
Read this if
You are wiring a subscriber, picking a RUST_LOG filter, pointing spans at a collector, or scraping /metrics

Where instrumentation comes from

Explanation. The emission sites, the compile-time gate they sit behind, and the two exits.

Two things leave a running SACI process. tracing events and spans go to whatever subscriber you installed, and on to an OTLP collector when one is configured. Prometheus metrics go to the /metrics route on the service's HTTP control plane. One value crosses between them: saci_stage_duration_seconds is measured from the lifetime of the pipeline.stage span.

the work being observed emission and export the processor, logging across the seam

The tracing feature

Reference. The compile-time switch, and the two fallbacks it leaves behind.

Both crates declare it, and it is off by default in saci-core (default = ["runtime"]). In saci-service the service feature includes tracing, and the saci-service binary requires service, so the shipped binary always has instrumentation compiled in.

TOMLas declared; the service list is abridged
# crates/saci-core/Cargo.toml
tracing = ["dep:tracing"]

# crates/saci-service/Cargo.toml
tracing = ["dep:tracing", "saci-core/tracing"]
service = ["saci-core/io", "distributed", "parquet-checkpoint", "tracing", "dep:saci-config", ...]
Constraint

This is a compile-time switch, not a runtime one. Every emission site sits inside #[cfg(feature = "tracing")], so with the feature off the call and its field formatting are absent from the binary. There is no disabled-level cost to pay, and emission cannot be turned back on without rebuilding.

Two sites keep a fallback for the feature-off build, because losing them silently would be worse than the dependency. HostIo::log falls back to eprintln! so processor log lines are never dropped, and DistributedRunner's claim-release path prints to stderr so a failed release is always visible.

Inside a .wasm processor the feature is never available: saci-processor takes saci-core with no default features and only its processor feature. A processor reports through the host-io imports instead: log and metric, which the host bridges into its own subscriber.

A processor's println! goes nowhere. The host builds each processor's WASI context with WasiCtxBuilder::new().build() and never calls inherit_stderr(). That builder's documented default discards everything written to stdout and stderr, so println! and eprintln! inside a processor vanish. host-io::log is the only channel out.

The spans and events, module by module

Explanation. The shape of the tree, then the exact names and fields.

Nine span names, plus flat events across the targets tabulated below. pipeline.run, pipeline.stage and system.execute come from saci-core's execution path at info, and task_attempt comes from the retry driver inside them, also at info but only on a retry. The host adds five, all at debug: workflow.batch around one iteration, source.drain, runtime.run, sink.write, and processor.batch around one out-of-process processor call. One whole tree of those five opens per item, so log_level="info" materialises none of them and log_level="debug" is what brings the per-item waterfall back. The default log_level="error" materialises no span at all.

Every host span carries workflow, the declared workflow id, and each node's span carries that node's declared id. Field names below are the exact keys the macros record, so they are what you match on in a JSON log pipeline.

TargetLevelsWhat it reports, and with which fields
saci_core::pipeline::execution info spans Three nested spans per run: pipeline.run with pipeline, stages and rows; pipeline.stage with stage (0-based) and systems; and system.execute with system, the name from SystemMeta. The parallel-stage fan-out re-enters the stage span inside each spawn_blocking closure, so a sliced system's attempts stay under the right parent.
saci_core::retry info span on retries, warn, error The task_attempt span at info, carrying attempt (1-based) and max_attempts. It opens only on a retry: a first attempt that succeeds opens no span, so a clean run produces none. Then a warn per failed-but-retryable attempt with error, attempt, max_attempts, delay_ms, and an error on exhaustion with error and attempts. Both the async and the blocking driver emit it, from one shared attempt counter.
saci_core::windows::system warn Rows dropped because their timestamp was null: component, time_field, null_count. Needs the windows feature too.
saci_service::service::standalone debug spans, info, warn, error One workflow.batch span per iteration with workflow, iteration and rows, one source.drain per source with workflow, source, component and rows, one runtime.run per processor with workflow, processor, rows_in and rows_out, and one sink.write per sink with workflow, sink, component and rows, in topological order. Every iteration event names the batch span as its parent, so the whole iteration is one trace. The busiest module.
saci_service::service::stream debug spans, info, warn, error The same span set per arriving item, minus source.drain: the wait for input precedes the item and would otherwise dominate its latency. Because those spans are debug and the default level omits them, every error and warning here names its own workflow, iteration and node rather than relying on a parent span's fields, and renders as a root record in the Logs tab. Events carry source, sink, processor and error.
saci_service::distributed::runner debug spans, info, warn, error One workflow.batch span per claimed batch with workflow, claim and rows, holding one runtime.run. Expired-lease sweeps and every release-instead-of-ack path: reclaimed_count, claim_id, error.
saci_service::distributed::consensus::transport::server info, debug, warn The Raft TCP accept loop: addr on bind, peer per connection, error on frame, decode and encode failures.
saci_service::distributed::parquet_checkpoint debug A parent-directory fsync that failed after a checkpoint write: error. Needs the parquet-checkpoint feature.
saci_service::wasm::host_impl trace to error The processor's own host-io::log lines, re-emitted at the level the processor asked for and tagged pipeline and target. They land inside that batch's processor.batch span, because the runtime re-enters it on the blocking thread the guest call runs on. A host-io::metric call records the saci_processor_metric histogram, labelled with the metric name, and also emits a trace event with metric and value.
saci_service::wasm::runner debug span, warn One processor.batch span per run-batch call, covering the IPC encode, the guest call and the IPC decode: workflow, processor, rows_in, rows_out, systems_run, retries, guest_wall_us, the last four read back off the WIT run-metrics record. The warn covers building the template dataset: describe() failed, or one component's schema would not parse (component, error).
saci_service::plugin::runtime debug span, debug The same processor.batch span for a native plugin, with plugin_wall_us in place of guest_wall_us. The debug reports a loaded plugin's plugin, version, stateful and components.
saci_service::service::http, ::shutdown info, debug, warn, error Control-plane bind and clean shutdown, signal receipt, and the 30-second shutdown budget being exceeded.
saci_service::commands::serve info, error Binary startup (node_id), which of signal-or-runner-exit fired first, and the exit path.
saci::flow_control info The adaptive-flow-control lines: flow control starting per governed source, flow control decision per episode, flow control finished per governed source at runner exit, and one naming each stream source a windowed path leaves ungoverned. The EnvFilter enables this target at info whatever log_level says, and the sampler never drops it, so admission control is readable at the error-only default.
saci::windowing warn One condition, per windowed processor node: every row of an arrival is beyond the node's allowed_lateness_ms, so no window opens or closes and its sinks receive nothing. One line opens the run and one ends it, and saci_window_late_arrivals_total counts every arrival in between. Enabled at warn whatever log_level says, and never sampled, because every other number reads healthy while it lasts.
saci::heal warn The connector self-healing lines, every one carrying workflow, node and role: connector heal scheduled adds attempt, delay_ms and consecutive; connector healed adds attempt; connector heal failed adds attempt and error; connector heal exhausted adds attempts, the configured maximum it spent; and connector recovered carries the three common fields alone. saci_connector_heals_total and saci_connector_heal_failures_total count the outcomes. Enabled at warn whatever log_level says, and never sampled, so the pair a heal produces is never split by a level filter.
tower_http::trace info, debug Not SACI code, but it is in the output: build_router installs TraceLayer::new_for_http(), so each request to /health, /ready, /metrics or /status gets a span and request/response events.

Spans nest, so a JSON log line carries its whole ancestry and a collector can reconstruct one trace per iteration. The host draws the outer three levels.

A native pipeline's pipeline.run nests three levels further. A processor opens the same three inside the guest, where the host cannot see them, so a WASM processor is one span rather than a subtree.

Installing a subscriber

Reference. What a library embedder must do, and what the binary does instead.

SACI never installs a subscriber for you when you use it as a library, so without one every event is discarded. The minimum is tracing-subscriber with the fmt and env-filter features.

TOMLpath dependencies: these crates are not published
[dependencies]
saci-core = { path = "../saci-core", features = ["tracing"] }
tracing-subscriber = { version = "0.3", features = ["fmt", "env-filter"] }
Rustinstall once, before the first pipeline runs
use tracing_subscriber::EnvFilter;

#[tokio::main]
async fn main() {
    tracing_subscriber::fmt()
        .with_env_filter(EnvFilter::from_default_env())
        .init();

    // build and run your pipeline; the pipeline.run span tree and any
    // window or runner events now reach stdout
}

The service binary does this for you. saci-service serve calls init_logging before anything else can emit, and treats a second call as an error because the global subscriber is already installed. It stacks the EnvFilter, then one sampled group holding the fmt layer, the inspector's capture layer and an OTLP layer when otlp_endpoint is set, then SpanMetricsLayer for the stage histogram. The group shares one Sampler, so stdout, the dashboard and the collector see the same sampled stream; the histogram sits outside it because metrics are not sampled.

Rustwhat the binary calls
use saci_service::service::config::ObservabilityConfig;
use saci_service::service::logging::init_logging;

let cfg = ObservabilityConfig::default();  // Pretty, "error", no span export
// init_logging returns the guard and the inspector handle, None when capture is off.
let (telemetry, _inspector) = init_logging(&cfg, node_id)?;

// ... run the service ...

// Flush exported spans. Dropping the guard is not enough, because
// set_tracer_provider keeps a clone in a process-lifetime static.
telemetry.shutdown().await;

When observability.otlp_endpoint is set, init_logging builds an OTLP/HTTP span exporter, appends /v1/traces to the collector root, and installs the tracer provider. The returned TelemetryGuard is load-bearing. Dropping it does not flush, because set_tracer_provider keeps a clone in a process-lifetime static. The caller must call telemetry.shutdown().await before exit. serve does that after the runner stops and before the last log line. Export covers spans only: metrics stay pull-only on /metrics.

The keys that drive all of it, the thirty-two series on /metrics and what the endpoint does not carry are on Logs, metrics and traces.
